# Spec checklist

Everything the specs describe, written by `scripts/spec_list.py`. **An automatic tick means a rule found evidence, not that anyone played it.** The tag on each ticked line names the rule. An unticked line may still be built: the rules are strict and only see plain text, so most built behaviour has no automatic tick. To confirm something yourself, change `[ ]` to `[x]`; a rerun keeps it while the line's text is unchanged.

**42405 items: 2349 ticked by a rule, 0 ticked by hand, 40056 open.**

| address in code | 559 | Every boot-data address on the line is read by the code |
| title named in code | 312 | A code comment naming this spec also names the section's title |
| answered | 198 | A spec answered the request |
| story check passed by teleport | 197 | The goal's Done condition held in the story check |

| a status note traces it | 31 | A status note says the step was traced |
| module does nothing | 7 | The spec says the module does nothing, and it has no code |

- [ ] SPEC-0016 Behavior
  - [ ] SPEC-0016 0. Conventions
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 0. Conventions: Distances are horizontal: d = sqrt(dx^2 + dz^2). Height is ignored everywhere except the engagement gate in section 5 (the hero's height).
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 0. Conventions: Percent rolls are integers from 0 to 100 inclusive; a roll is a success when it is less than the chance (SPEC-0014).
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 0. Conventions: The random generator is the shared one, seeded once from the console clock (SPEC-0014).
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 0. Conventions: A tick is 1/60 s. Level flags are set and cleared through the level's flag array (SPEC-0014).
  - [ ] SPEC-0016 1. Tick order
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: Play rate set to 1.0, and the invulnerable word of the serpent set to 1 (it is set on every tick and never cleared; see Hurt side, section 8A).
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: If the belch cooldown is above 0, subtract 1.
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: Health band check (section 2), under the state gate of section 2.
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: Engagement check (section 5), only when armed (always) and the same state gate allows it.
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: Anchor check (section 4), in the states of section 4 (idle, belch and arrive). It runs after step 4 and can replace the state step 3 or 4 jus...
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: Run the handler of the state that exists after steps 3 to 5 (sections 6 to 9); a state chosen this tick runs its handler this tick.
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 1. Tick order: Aim and presentation (not covered); then wait one tick.

  - [ ] SPEC-0016 11. Damage and effects
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 11. Damage and effects: Lunge: 20 to the hero, once per lunge, unreduced by the hero's defences; a blocked lunge deals nothing.
    - [ ] SPEC-0016, 11. Damage and effects: Stun strike: the integer returned by the hero damage query with multiplier 1.0, applied once per stun.

  - [ ] SPEC-0017 1. Setup (once, when the encounter starts)
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 1. Setup (once, when the encounter starts): Set the nest state to active (1). This happens before the scan.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 1. Setup (once, when the encounter starts): Clear the three spider lists and mark every slot empty.

  - [ ] SPEC-0017 2. Per-tick loop
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Tunable copy.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Spider count: every tick, each valve's count is set to its spider-count tunable.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Valve HP: each valve keeps a copy of the HP tunable it last saw. When the tunable differs from that copy, the valve HP is set to the tunab...
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Valve sweep , for valves 0, 1 and 2 in that order. Let N be the valve's spider count and L the number of living spiders among the first N...
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: If the valve is not destroyed and L > 0, its state becomes 4 (alive), whatever its state was.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: If the valve is not destroyed and L = 0 and its state is not 1, 2 or 3, its state becomes 1 (closed), and the countdown is set to 600 ticks.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Consequence: a fresh valve (state 0) goes to closed at once, when it has no living spiders.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Nest update. Let d be the number of destroyed valves.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: If d = 3, the nest becomes defeated (state 2).
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Otherwise the nest's animation playback rate is set to 1.2 to the power d (section 6), applied after the sweep.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Nest state.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Active (1): update each valve's state machine (section 3), valves 0, 1 and 2 in order.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Defeated (2): play the defeat animation (4) on the nest, if it is not already playing. The valve machines do not run after defeat.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Idle (0): not reached in the shipped game (see Nest state). No idle branch is run.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Presentation (High). The nest writes a debug text into its own character's debug text buffer: the nest state name (none, fighting, destroy...
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 2. Per-tick loop: Wait one tick.

  - [ ] SPEC-0017 7. Respawn cycle
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: Closed (state 1) for 600 ticks (10 s).
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: Opening (state 2) for the length of animation 1. The window opens when it finishes.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: Spawn (state 3). The spiders are revealed on the first tick animation 2 is playing and unfinished.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: Alive (state 4) on the next tick, while spiders are alive, until every spider in the valve's list is dead.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: When the last spider dies, the sweep moves the valve to closed (state 1), and the cycle repeats.
    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: The hit window stays open until a hit lands. Since a hit closes the window, at most one hit lands per cycle.

    - [ ] SPEC-0017, 7. Respawn cycle: Destruction on the third hit happens in the same tick as the hit.

  - [ ] SPEC-0021 Mistakes to avoid when porting
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Giving money only to the active hero or keeping a wallet per hero. There is one party wallet, plus a stash word for Act 2.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Reading coin values from the item text table. The table has a 10 NP coin with a blank price and a name; the values are 1, 5,...
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Capping the wallet, clamping a coin pickup at 0, or flooring a purchase. Only remove and give floor at 0.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Paying a stolen amount exactly. Amounts that are not multiples of 5 come back larger.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Giving carried NP to a Neopoint thief, or letting it keep the stolen money. The thief never holds it; coins left lying are d...
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Treating the steal as "50 percent". It is 50 of 101 draws.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Skipping the 50-slot item pool: without it the 25,000 NP chest pays all 25,000.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Charging Gill the Fence the quoted price instead of 500, or forgetting that the first Meridell arena win gives a shield (or...
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Using a pull or magnet for coins, or an expiry other than 11.2 s after launch.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Adding NP on death, charging a continue, or showing a persistent counter in play.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Starting Act 3 without the stash wallet, or Act 2 with the Act 1 wallet instead of exactly 1150.
    - [ ] SPEC-0021, Mistakes to avoid when porting: Using the money roll draw as 1 to 100 or 0 to 100: it is 0 to 99, compared strictly below the chance. The steal chance uses...

  - [ ] SPEC-0035 10. Canvas and drawing position
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: The front-end canvas is 512 pixels wide and 448 pixels high. Its width and height are stored in the boot program's data as...
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: Screen coordinates have their origin at the top-left of the canvas. X runs 0 to 511 and Y runs 0 to 447.
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: Drawing to the 12.4 fixed-point screen space:
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: X_screen = (x + 2048 - 256) x 16
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: Y_screen = ((y - 224) x S + 2048) x 16, where S is the global Y scale (1.0)
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: So the canvas centre (256, 224) maps to the screen centre (2048, 2048).
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: The 640 x 480 values seen elsewhere in the code belong to the 3D view, not to the UI. The UI uses 512 x 448.
    - [ ] SPEC-0035, 10. Canvas and drawing position: Overlay cells are drawn only inside a 10-pixel margin around the canvas (section 15.1).

      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: A smoothed follow (lerp, speed matching, acceleration, leash). The original moves only by the clip's root step and p...
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: A distance teleport. There is none; the only catch-up jump is the bumped-and-out-of-view rule of state 3.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: The leave rule. The petpet runs toward the camera and vanishes when out of view or on a touch; it does not test the...
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: Speeds: treating speed byte 0 as invalid (it means 0.5 key per tick), multiplying the per-key root by the key count,...
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: Turning by a fixed angle per tick, or turning while idle, in gait 0 or during the enemy notice. It is a 0.1 blend on...
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: The idle point relative to the hero's facing. It is ± 3 to 10 on world X and world Z.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: The follow point's side. It is + 1.5 along the hero's B1 = normalise(up × forward), 4.0 ahead.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: A rest between idle variants, or restarting a finished one-shot variant. The variant is re-requested every tick; one...
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: Kind 7's (and kind 8's) notice. Id 8 is missing and plays the hungry clip.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: The edge guard, navmesh confinement or character push applied to the petpet. It has none of them.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: Following during scripted walks. States 50 and 52 count as standing, so the petpet heads for an old idle point instead.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: Letting enemies or the hero hit it.

      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: Freezing it in conversations. It keeps moving; only T is held.
      - [ ] SPEC-0047, G9. What a port most likely gets wrong: The wild roam wait. It is always 60 ticks, not 1 to 5 seconds.

    - [ ] SPEC-0049, Quest steps and the journal: A row is ignored when its start flag id or its done flag id is -1.

  - [ ] SPEC-0049 Save and load
    - [ ] SPEC-0049, Save and load: Save: the bitmap is copied as a block of 93 bytes into the slot at offset 0x030.
    - [ ] SPEC-0049, Save and load: Load: the 93-byte block is copied back into the live bitmap. Nothing else is written per bit.
    - [ ] SPEC-0049, Save and load: Empty slot: its bitmap is zero.
    - [ ] SPEC-0049, Save and load: A load restores flag 337 (and every other flag) exactly as saved; the only setter of 337 is the pedestal puzzle in pack 1382.

- [ ] SPEC-0051 Layout
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x00 4 u32 Kind: 0 = main story, 1 = side quest (SPEC-0049). Not read by the map.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x04 4 u32 Start progress flag id (SPEC-0049). The row is skipped when it is -1.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x08 4 u32 Done progress flag id (SPEC-0049). The row is skipped when it is -1.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x0C 4 u32 Title text, copied to the icon as its label.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x10 4 u32 Objective text (journal only).
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x14 4 u32 Stage. Stage 0 gives no icon. Otherwise the marker kind is stage minus 1.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x18 4 f32 World position x.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x1C 4 f32 World position z.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x20 4 i32 Scene (area) id, or -1 for none.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x00 4 u32 Name text of the treasure (for example "Bogshot Treasure"). Zero on the 4 sentinel rows.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x04 4 f32 World position x.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x08 4 f32 World position z.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x0C 4 i32 Area id (0 to 73), or -1 on the sentinel rows. A row with area -1 is never listed as a treasure.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x10 4 u32 Held-map flag. Zero on disc. Set when the hero holds map i (section 10).
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x00 4 f32 World x (quest row x, or treasure x).
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x04 4 f32 World z (quest row z, or treasure z).
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x08 4 u32 Marker kind. Quest icon: stage minus 1 (0 or 1). Treasure icon: 2.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x0C 4 u32 Label text: the quest title (quest icon) or the treasure name (treasure icon).
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x10 4 runtime reference Quest icon: the quest row reference (nonzero = the icon has items). Treasure icon: 0.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x14 4 runtime reference Treasure icon: the treasure record reference (nonzero = the icon has items). Quest icon: 0.
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x00 16 4 f32 G0 = (a, 0, b, 1): column 0 of the transform; a and b are the world-x factors of screen x and screen y
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x10 16 4 f32 G1 = (0, 1, 0, 1): column 1 (height; never reaches the screen point)
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x20 16 4 f32 G2 = (c, 0, d, 1): column 2; c and d are the world-z factors of screen x and screen y
  - [ ] SPEC-0051, Layout: +0x30 16 4 f32 G3 = (tx, 0, tz, 2): column 3; tx and tz are the screen offsets in pixels

  - [ ] SPEC-0051 5. Pulses
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: Start at 4096. Each tick, add the step (starts at +50).
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: If the value would exceed 4300, set it to 4300 and make the step -50.
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: If the value would fall below 3900, set it to 3900 and make the step +50.
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: Start at 1.0. Each tick, add 0.03.
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: If the value exceeds 1.5, set it to 1.5 and negate the step.
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: If the value falls below 0.8, set it to 0.8 and negate the step.
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: Integer, value 4290, step +50: next value is 4300 (since 4340 exceeds 4300); step becomes -50. Next tick: 4250, step stays -50.
    - [ ] SPEC-0051, 5. Pulses: Float, value 1.45, step +0.03: next value 1.48. Then 1.51 is above 1.5, so the value becomes 1.5 and the step becomes -0.03.

  - [ ] SPEC-0054, Edge cases and error handling: A blocked orb is reflected only when the hero faces it; a hero who does not face the orb takes the hit even if the kinds match.

      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The charge distance is a draw of 5 to 15 units and the bite range is 5.0, so an attack from d > 20 never connects. A standing h...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The Giant's slot 1 is eligible out to 25 units (49 percent a tick), so a Giant that wakes 25 units from a standing hero usually...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: A dodge or hit reaction aborts the sequencer with no end path: no recovery countdown, and the slot keeps the cooldown drawn at...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The Drackonack's strafe approach runs at 26.5 u/s and circles at 7.5 u/s; the lock rule (wall contact gives 120 ticks without c...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: Alarm groups in the Abandoned Mines hold 1 to 3 hidden Drackonacks each (group 3 holds Giants that are not hidden); waking one...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: A strike that leaves the hero at 0 hit points sends the enemy to the victory pose (id 73, 116 ticks), then the default-state step.
    - [ ] SPEC-0064 What a port most likely gets wrong
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Treating the Drackonack bite as a normal swing. It is a run of 5 to 15 units at 24 to 30 u/s (Giant 11 to 14) followed b...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Steering the charge. The run keeps its heading from the choice tick and the bite hits only a hero who is still within 5.0.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: The cooldowns. The Drackonack's slots wait 240 to 420 ticks each; the Giant's 30 to 120.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Dodge rates. The Giant dodges 84 to 89 percent of swings and the Drackonack 49 percent; the dodge animation carries it b...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: The Giant's counter: 60 of 101 a tick on a hit makes a 50-damage charge almost certain when it is off cooldown.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Forgetting that hidden Drackonacks and Giants are hittable (cue word 1) and that the group wakes together.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Using the strafe machine for the Giant (it rushes) or the rush machine for the Drackonack (it strafes).
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: The backbiter: a facing hero halves the Drackonack's attack rolls, a hero looking away doubles the rate.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Playing the blocked-charge clip or the stun clips; kind-2 charges never enter them.

    - [ ] SPEC-0064 Edge cases for implementers
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The map search ignores class state: a hidden (state 8) Wizard casts at a waiting corpse in sight and, when finished, enters agr...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The roll is drawn every tick while a candidate exists and the cooldown is 0; do not roll once per cooldown.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The candidate's HP must be below its maximum. A corpse has 0.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: A Wizard casting while its recovery countdown is positive is delayed (the roll is spent).
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The cast sets all slot cooldowns to 0 at its end (the agro setter), so a bolt can follow the spell as soon as the recovery coun...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The map search can start while a bolt cast is in progress (it needs only the recovery countdown below 1, which holds during a c...
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: Slot 1 is a decoy: never choose it.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, Edge cases for implementers: The spell's lifetime is the distance plus 5 ticks, and only the chosen target is tested.

      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Running the map search only in agro: it runs in every state.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Letting a skeleton rise while the hero stands within 5 units, or with no clear-area test.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Choosing slot 1 or giving the bolt the Archer's speed 2.0: it is 1.0, with damage 50.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Using a single rate for the bolt clip: the strike runs at 1.5 until the bolt and 1.0 after.
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Forgetting that the cast ends in the agro setter (cooldowns cleared, group alerted).
      - [ ] SPEC-0064, What a port most likely gets wrong: Giving the Wizard the Archer's notice (awareness 65): the Wizard's is 100.
